disease_label_per_paper: Secondary syphilis with hepatitis and nephrotic syndrome
presentation_summary: 51-year-old man presented with 3 weeks of dull epigastric/periumbilical abdominal pain, several days of non-bilious vomiting, and 1 week of intermittent bright red blood per rectum.
He denied fever, loss of appetite, weight loss, urinary symptoms, chest pain, dyspnea, and diarrhea.
Comorbidities included diabetes mellitus and osteoarthritis; medications included ibuprofen, famotidine, and metformin.
On exam he was afebrile and hemodynamically stable, with many copper-colored papules and macules on the body including palms and soles, plus mild bilateral pitting pedal edema.
Labs showed nephrotic-range proteinuria, alkaline phosphatase 274 U/L, AST 50 U/L, ALT 91 U/L, normal bilirubin, and preserved creatinine.
Viral hepatitis, autoimmune, and metabolic liver workup were negative; chest radiograph and abdominal ultrasound were unremarkable.
Liver biopsy showed chronic hepatitis with mild activity and portal/periportal fibrosis; kidney biopsy showed immune complex-mediated membranous glomerulonephritis.
RPR titer was 1:1024. The diagnosis was secondary syphilis with luetic hepatitis and secondary membranous glomerulonephritis, treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units intramuscularly.
